summary: Pinned model evicted during backend connection cutover causes partial streaming outputs and embedding mismatch
description:
Issue summary:
During a scheduled backend connection cutover in us-east, several long-lived streaming sessions for customer LexaHealth lost their pinned model affinity and were routed to a degraded fallback variant. The client observed partial stream termination (stream closed mid-response), truncated generated text, and subsequent embedding requests for the same session returning vectors that did not match earlier context (quality discrepancies).

Impact:
- ~18 sessions for one enterprise tenant experienced truncated streaming responses over a 7-minute window (13:04–13:11 UTC).
- One-hour spike in token usage billed to the customer due to replays and retries.
- Customer reports a critical downstream quality regression (medical summarization pipeline).

Environment:
- Prod (us-east)
- Affected models: open-llama-13b-v2 pinned on tenant route; fallback was rw-instruct-13b-quant (quantized, different tokenizer behavior).
- Canary cutover of edge-proxy pool was in progress (scheduled maintenance).

Steps to reproduce (observed / deterministic):
1) Customer pins model open-llama-13b-v2 via route configuration.
2) Start streaming chat session and keep alive for >10 minutes.
3) Trigger edge-proxy maintenance (rolling connection restart on a small canary subset as per planned maintenance).
4) Observe streaming connection reset, subsequent requests from the same session routed to fallback model; streaming responses truncated and embedding calls later return vectors inconsistent with earlier session context.

Observed behavior:
- Pin eviction was not logged as an explicit model-unpin operation; routing layer silently selected fallback after connection rebind.
- Edge prewarm service attempted to warm fallback variant and returned partial HTTP/2 stream close (RST_STREAM) for active streams.
- KV cache keys for session were invalidated or missed during replay, causing embedding divergence.

Expected behavior:
- Pinned sessions should retain model affinity across edge connection cutovers; control plane should either preserve pin or return explicit 409/422 indicating pin loss so client can re-establish. Streaming sessions should be retried gracefully without truncation.

Initial logs/traces (key pointers):
- edge-proxy logs (edge-conn-logs-2026-03-13.gz) show connection handoff at 13:04:17 UTC and immediate RST_STREAM to several connections.
- Orchestrator trace id: trace-0a7f3c shows pin-consensus check returning "no-match" for a small cohort between 13:04:18–13:04:20.
- Serving-runtime metrics show increased cold starts for fallback model (rw-instruct-13b-quant) between 13:04–13:06.

Temporary mitigation applied by Support:
- Forced re-pin command issued for affected tenant routes at 13:20 UTC (control-plane action SUP-FORCEPIN-237890).
- Customer instructed to enable short client-side retry/commit semantics for streaming to avoid truncation (client patch recommended).

Next steps / requested actions:
- Engineering to reproduce in staging with controlled edge-proxy canary restarts and long-lived streaming sessions.
- Add explicit control-plane audit event when pin affinity cannot be re-established during connection handoff.
- Investigate KV cache preservation and embed consistency across rebinds.
- Assess billing impact and prepare credit proposal for customer if required.

Customer note: LexaHealth flagged as enterprise with SLA; they are currently pausing scheduled production runs until a fix is confirmed.

investigation_notes: Root cause hypothesis: during rolling connection cutover the edge-proxy returned a transient 5xx on the stream socket, triggering client reconnect. On reconnect, routing layer saw the connection absent and attempted to prewarm available variants; prewarm traffic raced with control-plane pin reconciliation. If prewarm wins, fallback variant becomes routable and session affinity is not restored, causing partial responses.

KV cache TTLs: observed some session keys expired or were not rehydrated on the fallback because key namespace differs between pinned variant and fallback quantized variant. Need to normalize cache keying across variant families.
Telemetry gap: no explicit control-plane audit entry created when pin affinity failed to rebind during connection handoff. This makes postmortem attribution harder.
resolution: Temporary workaround: forced re-pin and customer-side short retry guidance applied; immediate customer impact mitigated. Planned permanent fix: (1) control-plane change to emit audit event and block fallback selection until pin-check completes for active streaming sessions, (2) serialize prewarm vs. pin-reconcile in edge routing logic, and (3) align KV cache keying across compatible candidate variants. Patch scheduled for canary deployment 2026-03-18. Billing review recommended for credits against replays. Ticket remains open until canary patch verifies fix in prod.
